text:
support-liaison: heads up — customer ACME (#987654) reports p99 jump on text.generate in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-16T21:07Z, impact: intermittent 3.5-4.2s p99 (was ~1.2s). They say it started after this evening's maintenance.

mira: confirmed — cluster metrics show p99 surge at 21:02 UTC, cpu/gpu utilization normal but host io p99 climbed. correlates with driver rollout event.

jordan: repro attempt on staging with same payload — getting tail at ~3.8s when requests hit nodes with driver 535.43. staging nodes on 534.21 are fine. quick curl used: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate`

eng-infra-bot: rollout event: driver-upgrade 535.43 -> applied to pool gpu-usw2-prod at 2026-03-16T20:55Z (6/24 nodes so far).

asha: NVMe qdepth p99 on affected hosts spiked from 16 -> 256 during KV cache flushes. suspect regression in driver+kernel interaction causing hostfs stalls.

mira: snippets from iostat/nvme (trimmed): ```Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %utilnvme0n1        0.00    0.00  10.50  20.30  4096.00 10240.00   512.0    112.4  45.2  12.1  59.8  0.90  83.1```

jordan: quick smoke: toggled `GRACEFUL_CACHE_FLUSH=false` in runtime on one node -> immediate p99 drop to ~1.3s for that node. suggests cache flush path interaction.

support-liaison: customer on live calls, requested ETA/mitigation.

mira: mitigation plan proposed: 1) pause driver rollout (stop remaining nodes), 2) roll back 6 already-upgraded nodes to 534.21, 3) shift traffic away from upgraded hosts via routing policy, 4) enable cache-bypass on affected runtimes as temporary workaround.

jordan: executed step 1 & 3 — paused rollout and toggled routing for new requests away from gpu-usw2-prod-upgraded tag. routing change reduced traffic to bad nodes by ~95%.

eng-infra-bot: rollback initiated: rolling driver 534.21 -> nodes gpu-usw2-03,04,07,09,12,14 (progress: 4/6 complete).

asha: note — full rollback takes ~12 minutes per node; during rollback nvme writeback spikes expected. planning rolling one-at-a-time with health checks.

mira: after first 4 rollbacks + routing change the cluster p99 is back to ~1.2s, ACME confirms improvement. marking as mitigation successful for now.

support-liaison: told customer: "We identified a regression in the latest driver+host interaction. We paused the rollout, rolled back impacted nodes, and routed traffic to stable hosts. We'll keep you updated and follow up with a root cause postmortem."

sre-amber: creating incident ticket and allocating postmortem owners: eng-infra (asha/jordan) + eng-runtime (mira). adding runbook links and metric graphs.

jordan: next steps for debug: collect nvme smart logs, full kernel oops/jitter traces, driver perf traces, and reproduce minimal repro that triggers cache flush path. leaving `GRACEFUL_CACHE_FLUSH=false` disabled in prod? prefer to keep it off on routed nodes until full fix.

mira: agree — do not change global flag yet, keep targeted nodes patched. schedule bisect on next driver candidate with kernel + nvme driver toggles.

support-liaison: customer asks about SLA credit — noted, will coordinate with CS.

customer-acct-bot: ticket 987654 updated: incident mitigated, customer notified, follow-up postmortem requested.

sre-amber: wrapping up — incident severity lowered, keeping monitoring window open for 6 hours. assigned follow-ups: `ENG-INFRA-457` (driver bisect), `ENG-RUNTIME-191` (cache flush hardening), `CS-issue-72` (SLA comms).

mira: tl;dr — driver 535.43 + host kernel nvme path caused KV cache flush host-io spikes; immediate mitigations: paused rollout, rollback, routing, targeted cache bypass. will own RCA and remediation timeline.

jordan: logs + repro artifacts dropped into /incidents/4479012345/artifacts (links posted).

sre-amber: thanks all. closing chat stream for now — please add any late signals here. :white_check_mark:
